1.note: "Josephus for the Romans" (היוסיפון לרומיים) is de' Rossi's designation for Josephus' Antiquities, as distinct from the Hebrew Yosippon; the book/chapter numbers are those of his edition.

2.note: Yedidyah (Philo) here refers to the pseudo-Philonic Breviarium de temporibus published by Annius of Viterbo, which de' Rossi cites as 'his book On the Times' (seg. 95).

3.note: An allusion to Isa 28:7 turned around; the apparent sense is that these priests too were righteous and not dissolute, so righteousness alone does not account for the long span. The precise point is uncertain.

4.note: Read as the rabbinic oath formula 'By the [Temple] service!'

5.note: The print reads ch. 1 (פ"א); the passage on the pious of the nations is at the end of ch. 8 of Hilkhot Melakhim (8:11), so the number may be an error.
